date.as_written: samvat 518 māgha kṛṣṇa daśamyā tithau | uttarāṣāḍhanakṣatre || śubhayoge budhavāsare

purpose: merit transfer to the śivācārya patron, with his parents first and all beings, so that they reach Śivaloka
notes: The cataloguer marked the patron's name as corrupt (†ulphāsabhārakasya†). The reading 'Ulphāsa' + bhāraka (probably the Newar title bhāro) is tentative. He receives the merit of the copy and is probably the patron/donor, but the colophon has no explicit commissioning verb. 'bhaktāpura mahānagare tripurakocche' gives his residence (the Tripura quarter or palace of Bhaktapur). The colophon does not explicitly say the copy was made there; the catalogue's 'Place of Copying: Bhaktapur' is inferred from this. NS 518 Māgha (early 1398 CE) fits the joint rule of Jayasthitimalla's sons, which included Dharmamalla. A Vajrācārya scribe wrote for a Śaiva (śivācārya) patron, and the colophon ends with a Buddhist triratna invocation.
